The favored product comes from the unsubstituted CH2 enolate attacking, leaving an acidic alpha proton on the ester-bearing ring carbon (C9H14O3).

fm:organic:oc-1gnnsax.why: One C=C provides 2 pi electrons and the cationic carbon is an empty p orbital completing cyclic overlap. 2 pi electrons = 4n+2 with n=0 -> aromatic, the textbook reason this tiny cation is unusually stable. The 4-, 0-, and 6-electron counts are miscounts, and 2 pi electrons cannot be antiaromatic.

fm:organic:oc-1nni7r4.why: A 3H singlet near 2.1 ppm plus a carbonyl band and no aldehyde proton identifies a methyl ketone (CH3-C=O), i.e. 1-cyclohexylethanone, which is the Markovnikov hydration product made with Hg2+/H3O+. Hydroboration (disiamylborane or BH3) would give an aldehyde with a 9-10 ppm CHO; ozonolysis cleaves; Lindlar only gives an alkene.

fm:organic:oc-16yhmrn.why: Tertiary halide in warm methanol (polar protic, weak nucleophile, no strong base) = solvolysis: SN1 and E1 compete; substitution via SN1. SN2 blocked (tertiary), E2 needs strong base (absent).
